chunks: Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hanan, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every day?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, no.' He said: 'How negligent you are! Do you visit him every Friday?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit him every month?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit him every year?' I said: 'Sometimes.' He said: 'O Sadir, how negligent you are toward al-Husayn (peace be upon him)!' and he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common response of respect)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the frequency of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) engages Sadir in a dialectical exchange to correct the companions' tendency toward spiritual neglect (*jafā*) regarding the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). By progressively lowering the frequency from daily to yearly, the Imam illustrates that even annual visitation was insufficient for those who had grown distant, thereby establishing Ziyarah as a vital, continuous practice for maintaining spiritual vitality and communal identity within Shia tradition.
